==English== {{wikidata lexeme|L25}} ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:strengthenen<-en>>|tree=1}} From rare {{inh|en|enm|strengthenen}} (14th c.), from earlier {{m|enm|strengthen}} (12th c.), where ''-en'' is the infinitive ending. Probably the original form was reinterpreted as {{af|en|strength|-en|id2=inchoative}} around the time when the infinitive ending was being apocopated in late Middle English. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈstɹɛŋ(k)θən/|/ˈstɹɛnθən/|a=RP,GA,CA}} ** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Simplificationalizer-strengthen.wav|a=New Jersey}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-strengthen.ogg|a=Southern California with California Vowel Shift|IPA=[ˈstɹænθɛn]}} * {{IPA|en|[ˈstɹeɪŋ(k)θən]|a=pre-/ŋ/ tensing,US,CA}} * {{rhymes|en|ɛŋkθən|s=2}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To make [[strong]] or stronger; to add [[strength]] to; to increase the strength of; to [[fortify]]. #: {{ux|en|'''strengthen''' a muscle}} #: {{ux|en|'''strengthen''' a wall}} #: {{ux|en|'''strengthen''' one's willpower}} #: {{ux|en|'''strengthen''' one's authority}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 4-2|text=Let noble Warwick, Cobham, and the rest,{{...}}
With powerful policy '''strengthen''' themselves.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1851|author=Anonymous|title=Arthur Hamilton, and His Dog|url=http://gutenberg.org/files/10888 |passage=A little hardship, and a little struggling with the rougher elements of life, will perchance but '''strengthen''' and increase his courage, and prepare him for the conflicts and struggles of after years.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[empower]]; to give [[moral]] strength to; to [[encourage]]; to [[enhearten]]. #* {{RQ:KJV|Deuteronomy|iii|28|text=Charge Joshua, and encourage him, and '''strengthen''' him.}} #* {{RQ:Hough Purchase Price|chapter=I|text="A fine man, that Dunwody, yonder," commented the young captain, as they parted, and as he turned to his prisoner. "We'll see him on in Washington some day. He is '''strengthening''' his forces now against Mr. Benton out there.{{nb...}}."}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Liza Lucas|title=How to beat smoking, other bad habits with better self-control|url=https://www.cnn.com/2015/07/31/health/beat-smoking-other-habits-with-self-control-techniques-and-games/index.html|date=2015-07-31|passage=A review of addiction research, published in Trends in Cognitive Sciences, suggests mindful meditation '''strengthens''' self-control in smokers, even among those smokers who haven’t set an intention to quit.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251104105814/https://www.cnn.com/2015/07/31/health/beat-smoking-other-habits-with-self-control-techniques-and-games/index.html|archivedate=4 November 2025}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[augment]]; to [[improve]]; to [[intensify]]. # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[reinforce]], to [[add]] [[to]], to [[support]] {{gloss|someone or something}} #: {{ux|en|'''strengthen''' an army}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=1958 June|title=First Battery Railcars on B.R.|journal=Railway Magazine|page=419|text=Each half-section of the battery weighs about eight tons, and the two underframes had to be '''strengthened''' to take this weight.}} #* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Chandelis Duster|title=Biden and Trump touted what they’ve done for HBCUs at CNN’s debate. Here’s what their records show|url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/07/01/politics/biden-trump-hbcus-cnn-debate-reaj|date=2024-07-01|passage=In 2019, Trump signed the Fostering Undergraduate Talent by Unlocking Resources for Education (FUTURE) Act, a bipartisan bill aimed at '''strengthening''' HBCUs as well as other minority-serving institutions by providing $255 million annually.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251005053635/https://www.cnn.com/2024/07/01/politics/biden-trump-hbcus-cnn-debate-reaj|archivedate=5 October 2025}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/may/08/white-smoke-signals-election-of-new-roman-catholic-pope|title=White smoke from Sistine Chapel chimney signals election of new pope|date=2025-05-08|author=Angela Giuffrida and Harriet Sherwood|passage=A priority for the new pope will be to '''strengthen''' the church’s unity amid differing views and expectations within the institution and growing polarisation in the wider world.|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/Dufgu|archivedate=8 May 2025}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[substantiate]]; to [[corroborate]] {{q|a belief, argument, etc.}} #: {{ux|en|'''strengthen''' the cause}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To grow strong or stronger. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1914|author=Elizabeth Robins Pennell|title=Our Philadelphia|passage=my affection seems so superfluous that I often wonder why it should be so strong. But wise or foolish, there it is, '''strengthening''' with the years whether I will or no}} ====Synonyms==== * {{sense|to make strong or stronger}} See also [[Thesaurus:strengthen]] * {{sense|to augment}} See also [[Thesaurus:augment]] ====Antonyms==== * {{l|en|weaken}} * {{l|en|atrophy}} ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|enstrengthen|instrengthen|prestrengthen|restrengthen|strengthenable|nonstrengthened|unstrengthened|strengtheningly|unstrengthening |strengthen up|strengthener|strengthening plaster}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top-see|to make strong or stronger|fortify}} * Afrikaans: * Albanian: * Arabic: * Aragonese: * Armenian: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Cherokee: * Chinese: * Crimean Tatar: * Czech: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hawaiian: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Ido: * Ingrian: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Kannada: * Ladino: * Latin: * Latvian: * Lü: * Māori: * Middle English: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|уси́ливать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|уси́лить|pf}} * Serbo-Croatian: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tagalog: * Tok Pisin: * Turkish: * Welsh: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top-see|to animate|animate}} * Dutch: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Italian: * Latin: * Middle English: * Serbo-Croatian: * Swahili: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to augment}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Finnish: * German: * Italian: * Latin: * Māori: * Middle English: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to grow strong or stronger}} * Armenian: * Bulgarian: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * German: * Hungarian: * Ingrian: * Italian: * Latin: * Polish: * Romanian: * Serbo-Croatian: * Tok Pisin: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top-see|to reinforce|reinforce}} * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} ===References=== * {{R:Webster 1913}} {{cln|en|ergative verbs}}
